title: Enabling Data Reduction for Flash-X Simulations
problem: High-fidelity physics simulations like Flash-X generate large amounts of sparse simulation data that must be written to files, consuming significant storage space and bandwidth. Reducing file sizes while preserving simulation accuracy and visualization quality is challenging.
motivation: Reducing file sizes saves storage space and bandwidth, improves visualization tool performance, and enables higher-resolution simulation outputs for better analysis.
method: The authors integrated SZ3 and ZFP compression technologies into Flash-X and evaluated them on the Frontier exascale supercomputer. They implemented both lossless and lossy compression techniques, systematically studying the effects of compression accuracy levels and chunk sizes across different Flash-X simulation problems.
key_novelty: Integration of SZ3 and ZFP compression into Flash-X with systematic evaluation of lossless and lossy compression tradeoffs on exascale hardware.
contributions: Integration of SZ3 and ZFP compression technologies into Flash-X
Comprehensive experimental evaluation of lossless and lossy compression on Frontier exascale supercomputer
Analysis of accuracy variations and chunk size impacts on compression effectiveness
Guidelines for simulation developers to adopt compression strategies tailored to their specific problems

metrics.accuracy: compression accuracy preservation vs original simulation fidelity

primary_theme: Data reduction and compression for HPC I/O
